part.text: I've read the spec and the tests. Let me check the baseline — run the tests against the current implementation and look at the module setup.

The current code is passing all the tests — so this is a pure refactoring exercise: rewrite `markdown.go` to be more readable while keeping all 17 cases green. The current implementation is a byte-by-byte scanner that juggles 5 pieces of state (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`, `pos`) and uses `strings.LastIndex` tricks to detect list termination.

I'll replace this with a line-based parser: first apply emphasis, then classify each line as a header, list item, or paragraph, and render it with a dedicated helper.

part.text:
All 17 tests pass and `go vet` is clean. Only `markdown.go` was changed — no new files, and `markdown_test.go` is untouched. ## What I did The spec (`.docs/instructions.md`) is the classic refactoring kata: the original code worked but was hard to follow. The old implementation was a byte-at-a-time scanner juggling five pieces of state (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`, `pos`) and using `strings.LastIndex` comparisons against the whole document to detect when a list should close. The rewrite in `markdown.go` is a line-oriented parser: - **`Render`** splits the input into lines and classifies each one with a `switch` — header, list item, or paragraph — building output into a `strings.Builder`. The only remaining state is a single `inList` flag. - **`applyEmphasis`** isolates the up-front `__`/`_` → ``/`` substitution (bold first, so `__` markers are consumed before single `_`s are considered). - **`headerLevel` / `isHeader` / `renderHeader`** handle headers: 1–6 leading `#`s render as `…`; seven or more fall through to a paragraph, preserving the "h7 is a paragraph" behavior. - **`isListItem` / `listItemText`** handle `*` items; each item renders as a self-contained `
  • …
    • `, so closing a list is just writing `` — no more open/close bookkeeping across newlines. Refactor notes are included as comments per the spec's suggestion. One deliberate behavior change on untested input: a `*` mid-line no longer starts a list (the old code did, whenever the document contained any newline); only lines *starting* with `*` are list items, which matches standard Markdown and all the test cases.
